text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Xtreme Cooler, Large Ice Box, PU Full Foam Insulation, Stays Cool for Days, Portable Cool Box; Perfect for Camping, Picnics and Festivals We keep one of these in the house at all times next to the kitchen to use as an extension to our refrigerator. We use it for both cold and hot food storage. For cold storage you can put a couple gallon jugs of frozen water in the cooler and it will keep the temperature between 37F and 39F for several days. We use the cooler to thaw meat, party prep, seasonal cooking prep, and anytime we run out of space in the refrigerator after a trip to the grocery store, big box store, etc. For hot storage we use it for resting hot smoked meats after they have been taken off the smoker. Cleanup and disinfection is a breeze.

We used three of these on a weeklong desert camping trip to an art and music festival, temps in the low to high 90s. These babies definitely keep ice for 5 days. We had one of them under our shade structure up off the playa surface with wooden blocks and the other two we kept up on wooden blocks in a covered cargo trailer. The one under our shade structure was opened and closed quite a bit because it contained our fresh food. The other two had alcoholic drinks and were opened less often because we were consuming mostly water. We bought ice on the 5th day but there was still quite a bit of ice present in the melt water. The ones in the trailer had lots of ice but they weren't opened as much. We drained the melt water to use for shower water and only charged them with ice one more time before we left the desert, and we did so just because it was relatively convenient and we wouldn't be unpacking them right away when we got home. Great coolers especially for the price.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Xtreme Cooler, Large Ice Box, PU Full Foam Insulation, Stays Cool for Days, Portable Cool Box; Perfect for Camping, Picnics and Festivals

text_fidelity_a:
Fuzion Spinner Shark Drifting Kneeboard (Red) Parts of this review may be unfair - lets start there.
I reviewed this. All 240 lbs of me. The breaks did not work. I am thinking maybe they were not made to stop someone weight 250 lbs! In which case, the rating goes up. However, once I finished I held the brake with one hand and turned the wheels with the other - it waqsnt too easy, but the break was not great.

On the flat, this is dull. On a hill its scary - especially without brakes! You are very low to the ground. The wheels are small - this means hitting pebbles, cracks in the street etc will bounce you all over the place.

I saw another review lament about the parts not fitting together - that cheered me up, I thought I was doing something wrong! I was unable to get the parts to join seamlessly.
And the safety flag? I know that in my youth that would have been lost in the 1st 2 hours playing with this. It really should lock into place.

Drifting is sort of fun, but not for long. You need to be on a hill going down to get the most out of it, which is limiting and carrying it back up the hill is going to get old.

I would be extremely concerned about the safety of a child on this, and would be concerned about how much play would come from it - the small wheels really do limit it.
text_fidelity_b: Fuzion Spinner Shark Drifting Kneeboard (Red)

text_fidelity_a:
Condition 1 30” Case, Hard Lockable Storage Box, Water Resistant Plastic Travel Case, Protective Luggage with Foam Insert, Rebel Economy, 2041, 30.63"x11.52"x3.56" "Any product is only as strong as its weakest part." And the weakest part of this case are the latches. Although I didn't want to prove it to myself and ruin this Condition 1 case, the light plastic used and flimsy design will not hold up to any hard use.

I know that this is considered an "Economy Grade Case", but I wouldn't trust it to protect any expensive firearms. Please remember that "water resistant" doesn't mean "water proof", it should protect your weapon from rain but it can not be submerged. Also remember that any weapon stored either in a hard or a soft case will eventually rust and/or discolor unless it is allowed to breathe and air out on occasion. It is amazing how badly a stored firearm can look after being kept in a humid environment for any length of time.

Dropping this case on a hard surface will eventually cause the case to fail if anything of any weight is placed within it. That of course is not what this case is designed for and you shouldn't accidently drop it from anything above shoulder height. While this might provide adequate protection for inexpensive weapons I am always surprised when a manufacturer tries to enter into the lowest end of the market when their standard products already have a good reputation.
text_fidelity_b: Condition 1 30” Case, Hard Lockable Storage Box, Water Resistant Plastic Travel Case, Protective Luggage with Foam Insert, Rebel Economy, 2041, 30.63"x11.52"x3.56"

Forgun Fishing Rig Board Plastic Double Side Spring Hooks Storage Catch Holder Random At original purchase the delivery date indicated it would arrive in about two weeks. Then after ordering the delivery was adjusted out to six weeks.

I tried canceling the order, you can't normally with the vendor as they ship it from China and it takes long time.

Amazon directly could not cancel and the person on the phone just gave me a credit for the purchase.

Thus, the package with the item just showed up today.

Look again at the item page showing four holders. No, it is deceptive as this is really ONE holder and only if you read the description carefully do you see it is one you are purchasing, not the four they show.

The item I received does not old leaders in place as the sliding hook where the leader is attached pops open so the spring won't hold.

This thing is junk and a reason buyers should be told where the order originates and it should be easier to get rating on the vendor. If you click on the vendor, "Forgun" it does not go to the vendor but instead lists "for gun" and products suggested by this description.

Deceptive over and over and Amazon needs to better manage these foreign sellers selling junk

text_fidelity_a:
Thule Raceway Pro Trunk Bike Rack This is clearly a sturdy, well constructed bike rack. There's no reason to fear that it will come loose on long trips.

Unlike most other bike racks it uses tight ratcheting cables for mounting to your car instead of fabric straps. Does that make a difference? Probably not. I've had a Saris Bones rack for over two years with about 1,000 miles on it -- I've never had a problem with it.

Unlike the Saris Bones it does not have side straps (just top and bottom of the trunk). But, more of the rack's surface area is pressed against your car, so the side straps are probably less necessary.

Mounting to your car: Very simple. Once you get the hang of it, it will maybe take 2 or 3 minutes. And it's a one man job.

While it should be able to fit on practically any kind of car, before buying you should still consult Thule's website to confirm that it will fit on your car. They have a very long list of cars that it has been rated to fit onto.

Attaching your bikes: Also very simple. It takes just seconds.

As for the "patented No-Sway Cage prevents bike-to-bike contact," yes it works, but plenty of other bike racks are built to prevent mounted bucks from swaying into each other.

Storage: It folds up flat, so it doesn't take up too much space in your trunk.

Competition: Thule's major rival in the field of bike racks is Saris. I don't think you can go wrong with the Thule, but to some degree it feels over engineered. Saris' design is much simpler, and significantly cheaper (though the Saris is hardly a budget rack). The only advantage I'd give the Thule over the Saris is its ability to quickly fold flat. So I'm taking a star off because I feel that price is unnecessarily high -- you can get the same level of performance from the Saris at a lower price.
text_fidelity_b: Thule Raceway Pro Trunk Bike Rack

I got these to replace the large oversized nail style stakes that I've been using for years. The big nails work, but they are sometimes difficult to insert and remove and are overkill for my needs.

For general use, I think these aluminum stakes are the perfect balance between the thin pin-like stakes that come with tents and the large nail stakes. The pack of 20 gives me enough for my 6 person tent and several spares.

I like the hexagonal shape of the stakes. I expect the size and hex shape will help prevent the stake from spinning around (a problem with the thin pin-like stakes). The shape of the hook itself should also prevent spinning.

I look forward to putting these in the dirt!

Update: After a weekend camping I think these are great for soft earth like in a campground or yard. In rocky ground I expect these will bend. For sandy ground I think I would want longer stakes.

But for normal earth these are great. They are better than the thin wire stakes that come with the tent, and yet small enough to store in the tent bag. I'm glad to have these.

text_fidelity_a: Ozark Trail 12-Person 3-Room Instant Cabin Tent with Screen Room (Orange) I literally looked at every single tent that was 4 stars or higher and slept at least 8 people or more.  We are 6 in our family but we always seem to have the neighbor kid wanting to stay over or my daughter's and son's friends.  So we tend potentially need room for at least 8 but would be better to have a 12 person as it gives room for more than 3 queen size mattresses.  We actually had 4 queens and a twin mattress in there.  Kids just had to roll from one to the other while we had little station areas setup in each room for the kids to have their laptops/ipads and even a small 32 inch tv.  Yeah I know it is not real raw camping it is in our backyard but still it is fun. Strung lights up along the way. Bought some 2 way radios for all of us to communicate while the kids and my teenage son stayed out in the tent.  We even have an extra Air conditioner we may use at some point if it is too hot in the tent.  I like the fact that it does not let water in.  The way the door area zips up it has a lower lip if you will that gets pulled upwards to create sort of a ledge that stands so the water cannot leak on the ground up into the tent.  If you keep all the windows and doors zipped, there are protective sheer pieces that zip up the windows, that keeps the water out as well.  We had a pretty bad rain/wind storm about 2 weeks ago.  I looked out and saw the tent was collapsed.  Not a thing wrong with it. Wife and I went back out after it let up, popped the tent right back up.
text_fidelity_b: Ozark Trail 12-Person 3-Room Instant Cabin Tent with Screen Room (Orange)

text_fidelity_a:
SPRI Short-Handle Speed Jump Rope First off, I'm not good at jump rope, and am a total newbie. the last time I used a jump rope was when I was about 10 - over 40 years ago! I am hoping to use this as another cardio alternative at the end of my weight lifting workout.

This is a decent rope, and does the job once you figure out the correct length. I did some googling, since nothing about sizing came with this rope and discovered that for sizing, all rope lengths are measured from handle tip to handle tip, NOT just the length of the cord. To determine the exact length for an individual, stand on the center of the cord. The handle tips should reach your armpits, or just below the shoulders. To adjust this jump rope you'll need a small philips head screw driver and wire cutters.

The problem I had with the adjustment is that I'm just 5'2" so had to shorten it quite a bit. this left a long length of cord hanging off one handle as you can only adjust one side. I now need wire cutters to cut it down to size because the rope is not just vinyl, it is steel wires that have a vinyl coating. It hurts when it slaps against unprotected feet (wear shoes!) and shins. I won't be trimming it completely the first time as I may need to adjust the length again as I use it more and get used to it.

I suppose if I was more experienced at jumping I'd probably give this 4 stars, but I'm still trying to get the hang of it and not sure right now if it is me or the rope. I may come back and change the rating as I get more experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: SPRI Short-Handle Speed Jump Rope

text_fidelity_a:
Topeak Explorer Rack I will first say the build quality of the rack seems good, and if you can get it mounted correctly to your specific bike, it will likely be a good rack for you.

However the rack could have been designed to fit more bikes better with a little more forethought. The product description says this rack is 16 x 14.5 x 9 inches. Maybe it is, however the critical dimension is the length of the support post for tire clearance reasons. The distance from the center of the bolt hole on the bottom, to the bent bar on top - ie the clearance measurement - is 14 and 15/16 inches. A 29er tire radius is obviously 14.5 inches, so if you were to mount the bottom of this level with your axle bolt you would have only 7/16 inch clearance - less than half an inch. Most rack mounting holes are well above the axle point, but some are not much. I was using P-clips since my frame has not rack holes, and even though I was completely free to mount wherever I wanted, I had trouble finding a usable position with much clearance. Since most 29ers are used in the mud at least on occasion, a little more clearance would have been nice.

Secondly, the hardware included is stainless M5 x 0.8, and there are just enough assuming your frame has the proper mounting holes. If your using P-clips or any other method, a trip to the hardware store will be required, and you likely won't find stainless hardware in metric. It wouldn't have killed them to add an extra bag of hardware for other bike mounting methods.

Lastly, if you plan to use the Topeak accessories for mounting then the top of the rack will be great for you. If your not, the top of the rack is not flat like most racks (because of the MTX grooves for easy accessory mounting). If your not using topeak bags and such, you should still be able to make it work fine, its just not flat.

Unfortunately there aren't many racks out there yet for 29ers, so this still might be a good fit for many.
text_fidelity_b: Topeak Explorer Rack

text_fidelity_a:
ALEX Toys Little Jumpers Trampoline 786 I do not recommend the Alex Little Jumper Trampoline unless space is an issue. For $23 less you can purchase the significantly larger and more stable [[ASIN:B008BIV87M Bazoongi 48" Trampoline Bouncer with Easy Hold Handle Bar - Sunshine Yellow. Special Exclusive Limited Edition]].

The instructions are worthless. For example, one part states to "attach the bungee cord to the cord lock by pulling the knotted end of the cord tight". Can I just start by saying "What?" Well there is no knotted end, so you have to create it, though it doesn't really tell you how to do that. Then you have the issue of only three helpful images for the entire manual. And I probably need to start by saying I like to consider myself rather capable when it comes to assembling items and frames of structures having helped my father build our homes and additions. The instructions also do not elaborate where the knotted end should go in reference to the trampoline itself. You can figure out where it needs to go in the medal cord lock, but not on the trampoline itself. The only picture shows half of the trampoline having the cord wrapped around it so you are left wondering what the starting point looks like.

I hazarded a guess and just went with it at that point. Once I wrapped everything around and made sure that I pulled the cord tight several times I then tied it off. The instructions are then once again really vague; therefore I knotted the last end of the cord by itself and pulled it through the medal fastener. I then proceeded to knot the last end of the cord that I had just wrapped around with the beginning part of the cord to ensure an additional sense of security. The instructions mention nothing of this but after looking at the final results, with pieces of cord jutting out in random places, I knew that my three youngest would see that as an invitation to mess with it. So I knotted both ends together, and I did that twice. My kids can be rather problematic.

The directions then tell you to place the cover on the trampoline, making sure that it fits. Once again, the instructions lack on details. They do not specify that the cover should be placed in a specific direction. I used the writing on the cover as an indication for direction, placing the writing outwards where the handle will go. Otherwise, the cover does not fit. I found this out through trial and error, of course. There are also plastic clips that apparently must be clipped to the trampoline in some fashion, that you obviously have to figure out on your own. The most obvious thing was to clip them to the bungee cords that were wrapped around the trampoline.

The next step is to secure the handle. And yet again, those wonderful directions prove that they are pointless. I finally just put the small yellow bar into the curved handle portion (not attaching to the trampoline base yet) to get a sense of where it should go in the actual trampoline frame. I was then able to figure out which direction it faced, knowing that screws would be added at the end. REALLY not clear, but I was able to figure out having put together dozens of pieces before.

All in all, given that it was purchased at a discounted price, it will work out fine in addition to our other in home trampoline. This might be alright for one child, but it would definitely not work for my three kids (4 yr old twins and a 2 yr old) if I did not have the second larger trampoline. They are the ultimate test in terms of durability for any toy and this one is unfortunately not built for heavy duty usage. This might be fine on its own for occasional use from a calmer child, which none of mine are.
text_fidelity_b: ALEX Toys Little Jumpers Trampoline 786

I bought the supports, then the Big Mouth so I can haul my road and off road bike, and then I had to shell out for the fairing because of the howling wind noise.  The major issue is that when you combine all three you have to begin modifying.  Due to the straps from the fairing, the long levers that hold the Big Mouth and the long bike strap levers all get in the way of each other.  To solve this issue I had to cut off half of the bike strap lever AND (since that wasn't enough) I had to cut off the lever that secures the Big Mouth to the supports.  In the end, it's a good product made less than average because Thule obviously didn't try it with different combinations of their other products (which you'll be forced to buy - ugh) and that's frustrating...for a product to be great it comes down to the details and no need for the customer who paid $$ to put in extra work to make things work...Thule has yet to figure this one out.

text_fidelity_a: Bushnell Banner Illuminated Crossfire 500 Reticle Riflescope, 4-16x 40mm I wanted a decent scope for a .223 Saiga, which surprised me by its accuracy...  Nothing too expensive, but nothing that was going to break in a few weeks or not hold zero.  I was quite pleased with my Bushnell Powerview 8x21 compact binoculars, and read many good reviews about the Bushnell Banner series of scope.  I bought this with reasonable expectations, and the Bushnell Banner 4-16x40mm Illuminated CF 500 Reticle Rifle Scope blew my expectations away.  I have a Nikon 4-16x50mm Monarch on my Remington, and I was impressed at how similarly the Bushnell performed.  It feels like a rock-solid build, all moving parts feel as smooth as glass on glass, the tube was perfect for my mounting hardware, and the optics...  Honestly, I think the Bushnell's optics are just as good, if not a little better.  The Banner CF 500 has a smaller objective lens than the Nikon Monarch, yet they're the same brightness in all of my indoor and outdoor tests.  The clarity is the same, and the reticle is brighter.  The only thing the Nikon excels at, is a broader eye relief (though the Bushnell still has a fair range at the lower magnifications) and the controls are just a tad more precise (I have to fine tune the Bushnell a few seconds more - though maybe it's just because it's still new to me).  For the money, I think this Bushnell Banner 4-16x40mm scope is a great buy.  For my purposes, I don't feel it lacks at all.
text_fidelity_b: Bushnell Banner Illuminated Crossfire 500 Reticle Riflescope, 4-16x 40mm

text_fidelity_a:
Contigo Superior 2.0 Stainless Steel Travel Mug with Handle and Leak-Proof Lid, Double-Wall Insulation Keeps Drinks Hot up to 7 Hours or Cold up to 18 Hours, 20oz Juniper When I order a product I am more interested in the negative reviews than the positive ones. What problems are other people having? Do the buyers understand how the product works or are they misusing it? Are there design errors in the product? Does it function as advertised? Is it possible that a string of bad reviews is due to a switch in manufacturers? That by the way is often the case and a company has to own that choice.

My first use resulted in an unintended torture test. After filling up the mug with my first cup of coffee in the morning -- when I am still a bit fumble fingered -- I dropped the full mug on our marble floor. You know that moment when the dropped item appears suspended in the air and you are anticipating a horrible crash and the resulting mess? Didn't happen here! Boy was I relieved. I hate to catch flak from my wife to start the day.

Since my wife will be using this mug on her commute to work I was most interested in the claim that it would keep liquids "hot for up to 7 hours". So I filled it up with hot coffee at 10:00 pm and opened it this morning at 7:00 am. For the mathematically challenged, which most of the younger kids seem to be these days, that is nine hours. When I popped the lid one-handed (which takes a bit of practice) and took a sip, I was rewarded with coffee that was better than warm but not quite hot.

Most users of course will not use this as a thermos to keep something hot or cold for 8-10 hours. Instead they will be steadily drinking/sipping from the cup until the beverage is finished. Constant repetitive opening and closing of the tab is bound to release heat faster and the remaining liquid will no doubt be at less than a desired temperature, but it was nice to see that it would function as promised.

So Contigo got it's act together, either by changing something in the product or finding a better manufacturer. The mug is a subtle pleasing color and fits perfectly in our vehicles. The lid opening mechanism comes stiff and takes a bit of use to work it loose. Even though the company says that you can put the lid (only) in the dishwasher, I always get better long-term results by hand washing them. Made in China.

text_fidelity_a:
EKTOS 90% Woolen Blankets, 90" x 66", Warmest Blanket, Washable Wool Blanket, US Navy Blanket (Navy Blue) My dog likes to sit in my lap when we're by the campfire. I purchased this to cover her up and protect her from any stray sparks & pops. It is FABULOUS. We used our old blanket (an old synthetic bed cover) for years but it was in no way fire retardant and it took one good spark to make the blanket smoke. It was extinguished quickly but my dog was not comfortable near the fire afterwards. (I know it was ignorant to use a synthetic blanket next to a campfire but I grabbed it heading out the door for our first camping trip and since it worked didn't change it. DERP)

After our fiasco, my dog was scared of fire so I decided to purchase something wool and after careful consideration ended up with the Ektos blanket. Best purchase ever! She loves the blanket and is on my lap again. I love the blanket too. It is heavy but not overwhelming and not nearly as scratchy as other reviews made it out to be. Mind you, I'm not laying my bare skin against it. Bet it would be uncomfortable if I were wrapped in it half nekkid and sweating ...but I'm not, so it is perfect for what we're using it for. Both myself & my dog have piece of mind using this blanket as something of a campfire shield for her.

9/7/2018 Update

My husband used our campfire blanket as an extra layer to sleep in. He said it was perfect so I just ordered another blanket for him!

The original blanket I purchased is obviously still in great shape & being used regularly. I wash it on delicate and put it in the dryer on extra low. The first dry will produce a good deal of lint but the lint tapers off after that. It has been washed several times and has softened up a bit since purchase. I suspect we will end up purchasing a few more of these over the next few years since it is so hardy and versatile.

I would absolutely recommend this blanket others.

5/17/21 Update
...and I'm back to purchase yet another blanket! In a pinch, I had to use one of my campfire blankets in my hammock. It worked so well I am picking up another one to store with my hammock gear (along with another underquilt). Old Ektos are still go with us on every camping trip!
text_fidelity_b: EKTOS 90% Woolen Blankets, 90" x 66", Warmest Blanket, Washable Wool Blanket, US Navy Blanket (Navy Blue)

text_fidelity_a:
Allen 102S Premium 2-Bike Trunk Mount Rack I placed this bike rack onto my 2003 Nissan Sentra. I knew this was the correct rack to buy thanks to the website that provides a list (Visit the fit list FIRST before purchasing an Allen bike rack): [...]

Anyway, since this bike rack had such good reviews and it was the right one for my car, I decided to buy it. Hooking it up was fairly easy. I'll admit, I struggled a little bit only because it was my fist attempt, but I know that it will be a peace of cake from now on. Once you get it right the first time, the future attempts will be perfectly easy. When I was finished, I put my body weight onto it to ensure it was sturdy enough for a bike, and it was definitely safe! That bike rack was not going to go anywhere! The straps and everything ensured it was sturdy and safe for the road!

I had to pick up my new bike today (A Schwinn Riverside 26" female bike that looks like this: [...]. As you can tell by the photo, my bike is a female bike. Because it is a female bike WITHOUT a straight bar, I had to purchase a second part that is also by Allen seen here: http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B000ELSSZE/ref=oh_details_o00_s00_i00. This bar is easy to install as well. It took me about ten seconds to place it onto my bike securely. This allowed me to easily put my bike onto the rack without any issues. Keep in mind, this is only for bikes that do NOT have a straight bar. You may or may not need this part. I needed it for mine.

Once I placed the bike onto the rack, I tightened up the straps. One thing I noticed is that the front wheel of the bike was not secure. It was free to turn as I drove, which would bang into my car, so I simply got a bungee cord and wrapped it in a way to prevent it from moving while I drove. I also got a bungee cord for the back wheel to prevent that wheel from spinning (this is not necessary, but I just prefer to do this). The peddles of the bike hit the bumper, so I would also recommend socks or clothes of some sort to be wrapped around them so they don't scratch the paint of your car.

Anyway, my bike and I made it home perfectly fine. The bike was very secure and sturdy on the bike rack. That bike was not going anywhere, even though I went up and down hills and made a lot of turns on my way home at around 50mph. I have not gone on the highway with it yet, but based on my experience so far, I am certain it is fine.

Overall, I recommend this product! It's great!
text_fidelity_b: Allen 102S Premium 2-Bike Trunk Mount Rack

Bike Mirror Camera with 4.3 Inch Screen and 145° Wide Rear View Angle,Clear Night Vision,Perfect Bicycle Accessories for Mountain,Road Bike Trailer This is a very cool camera. . . but. . . there are a few things to know. . .

#1. There’s not only is plastic covering on the screen… There is also a tiny plastic cover that needs to be removed on the camera itself.

#2. Make sure you watch the video for installation instructions. This information is not in the packaging.

#3. Make sure you turn/adjust the camera before tightening. Though you can turn the screen anyway you like, it’s best to rotate/adjust the camera 1st to make sure it is in the right position and level before you start rotating the screen.

#4. Though there are buttons on back of the screen, there are no labels on the buttons. Though there is information in the instructions, it is not clear and does not give you much information. You really just have to play with it to see how it will works. But to be honest, I was quite happy with the settings as they were from the start and did not tinker with anything.

#5. The screen is charged using a micro USB cord. One is included, but a wall charger is not included.

#6. It takes a couple of seconds for the screen to turn on after you press the power button. Also, you are not to turn the screen on until after you have plugged the camera cable in.

I’m quite impressed with the quality of the picture. It is very clear. It shows that it’s 1080 P and I assume that’s correct.

This is a “generic” bike rearview camera. There is no branding on the box. So it could be sold by any number of different companies. It is made in China.

text_fidelity_a: Miken Ultra II SSUSA Bat All you have to do is go to any senior softball park and look at the bats in the rack.  Miken Ultra II is the most popular bat in the game.  It is not eligible for leagues other than senior softball because it is so good at making the ball pop off the bat.  That extra ball speed makes for a more dangerous hit.  So the bats are restricted to just old guys.  I have and still own 6 or 8 models of Miken bats and the Ultra II is the best model for most batters.  In 10 years I have had one bat crack.  I still use it for swinging practice.  If you like an end loaded bat, check out the other models.  But don't buy this crap about no warrenty.  If you are worried about breaking your bat, buy an old 50oz aluminum bat and hope you get the ball out of the infield.  If you want to be competitive and can afford the best, buy the Ultra II.  If I was to bet, I would say those with negative posts are shills for the competing manufacturers.  I have no connection with Miken other than liking to use products that help us old men hit the ball farther.
text_fidelity_b: Miken Ultra II SSUSA Bat

I really like how this device encourages great posture and discourages hyper-extension of joints. Push-ups would be a nearly perfect exercise if people didn't hyper extend their joints or over strain their weak parts when doing them. This device fixes everything by using your body weight to give you exercises that you can actually do.

This has helped me a ton with my upper body strength. It works, and I definitely recommend it.

Now, for the negatives.

The tension bands are a joke. Unless you either cut them apart or use all 65 lbs of them, they'll make a horrible snapping noise. You'll end up just throwing these away.

This won't last forever. It's not the sturdiest construction, and the design puts some weird strains on some of the joints, so it's only a matter of time before this falls apart. But you should get about a year of good use out of it, and by that time you'll be doing push-ups on your own.

The legs/feet of this should have been about twice as long, to make this sturdier. As it is, the only balanced position is with the seat placed on my upper stomach. If they were longer, then I could pick where I wanted to place my body on this.

And dismounting takes a lot of practice, and the fabric part peals off the first day you use it.

But overall, I'd heartily recommend it, especially if you've always dreamed of being able to do a lot of push-ups. No matter what your fitness level, this will definitely push you to the next level with push-ups.

Pros:
+Great way to work up to doing push-ups
+Great way to rapidly increase the number of push-ups you can do
+Fits away easily in a corner
+It's sturdy enough for what you need it for

Cons:
-You won't ever use the tension bands
-It's not the sturdiest construction. Expect it to break after about a year of use.
-Comes with fabric that's warping and pulling off
-The legs should have had more surface contact with the floor, to make this more steady
-I fell off this quite a few times when trying to stop doing push-ups, so it will take some time to get used to dismounting this device
text_fidelity_b: Push-Up Pump

text_fidelity_a: Reebok Adjustable Weighted Belt I used the belt for the first time today, after the particular weight vest I bought turned out to be a total loss (and cost me $12 to return to Amazon, thank you very much).  This belt was an improvement, but that's not saying much. To begin with, the strap that attaches to one end of the weighted tube appears to have been sewn or attached vertically, rather than horizontally.  This means that when you attach the belt to its fastener on the other side (which is attached properly-i.e. horizontally), the strap is twisted. So there is minor discomfort even before you've done any exercise. The belt does cinch nicely, and shifts just slightly side-to-side during (my relatively mild) walking exercizes- however, I did not try any moves that involved jumping up and down, specifically because I was afraid that the weight would bounce up and down and be very uncomfortable .  The darn thing is just bulky- about as big around as a water bottle, and rests right along the hips. All the weight is in the back, which throws off your stride- also, you can't move your arms very freely,and you have to make a pretty conscious effort to keep your swinging elbows from whacking the thing each time you stride.  I may try it a time or two more on days when I am only doing moderate walking exercizes, but I'm probably going to return it and try to find a decent vest that will stay put during exercize and not choke me.  It is ironic that the initial 5 lb. vest I bought at TJ Maxx 2 years ago has been far and away the best device I've used for loading the body during exercize.

Last, the materials themselves seem okay, but by no means strong enough to last a long time. The pieces that snap in - by virtue they are already not in - seemed like they could snap if we fought to get them in. We did try - they did not snap - but there was no way to do it. ABSOAR Cycling Bike Lights Front and Rear Silicone LED Water Resistant Headlights Tail Light High Intensity for Safety, 2 Pack Most headlights have a lens that casts forward, to amplify the LED(s) so that you can brightly see what is in front of you. This lens arrangement offers little-to-no side exposure to alert side drivers of your presence.

These lights are visible from the front or back (depending on your placement) PLUS from the sides.

I bicycle with four lights, solid and strobing white lights in the front and solid and strobing red lights in the back. Each of the front and back light has side strobe exposure.

I also wear a neon yellow reflective vest and drivers still turn right into me. I know to brake hard at a moment's notice and that knowledge has probably saved me an injury at least a few times.

After I brake hard and raise my hands in the air to say "WTF," the driver says, "I DIDN'T SEE YOU." Me, with all this regalia of lights and reflective strips on my vest, "Seriously?"

Drivers just don't think. They just turn the wheel and apply pressure to the foot controls.

Just do the best you can and make certain that you have side light coverage.

My application doesn't require food to be flung far. I have a plastic shield in front of the unit to keep the feed under the feeder. Without the shield, it tosses the feed approx 10'.

At purchase time:
Setup was pretty easy. A 5-gallon container, drill a couple of holes, add a pulley and some thin cable and you're in business.

I've had this feeder for approx 5 months. I first tried small dog food, but it clogged. Now I use small cat food and if I tilt the feeder towards the release area, it doesn't clog at all. Make sure the food is dry and you keep the lid on.

The timer works extremely well. I change it fairly often because I want to feed just after dusk and then a few more times during the night. Some feedings are 3 seconds, some are 4 seconds. 2 seconds seems to not be long enough and clogs the feeder. Atleast with the food I'm using. I have a camera on the feeding area, so I can say for sure the timer works very well.

If you have failures, you need to look at the spinner area and verify you have a clog or that the food isn't feeding down to the spinner, don't blame the timer, it's the food. Either too big or clumping.

text_fidelity_a:
Thule 9001 Raceway 2 Bike Trunk Mounted Bike Rack, Black, One Size 3000 mile round trip with 2 road bikes at 85mph and we couldn't be happier. It took me about 3 minutes to figure out the install and another 3 minutes to load up the bikes. The rack holds extremely steady with virtually no movement from the bikes and requires little, if any, tightening once underway. Just as other user mentioned, we did have some damage to the lower bumper, a slight indention and a little peeling of the clear coat, but I don't hold that against this product. Really its just the ABS plastic bumper that was the issue and its hardly a problem. As for the trunk lid, there was absolutely no damage or markings at all. The color of the product is slightly misrepresented in the pictures - its more of a flat, colorless black composite than a shiny black color. Again, this is no issue for me, just not exactly what I expected. I will say, I'd guess this product could easily be painted to match your vehicle if you really wanted a cool, custom look. One other unexpected issue was the loss of MPG. We were driving a Honda Civic that regularly gets 30+mpg and that fell to 25-27mpg. Once more, no issue with the product, just something to be aware of for those on a longer drive.

On the whole, this rack is super easy to use, looks a LOT nicer than other racks, heavy enough to feel solid, light enough to store with ease. Over he course of our 3000 mile journey, I took this on and off 6 times and I never begrudged doing it. I would highly recommend this bike rack to anyone that asked.

Tips: Make sure the points of contact are clean before putting the rack on. This will ensure no dirt gets trapped and acts like sand paper once moving. Use small bungies or velcro straps to secure your front wheel from spinning and one more to secure the pedals of the two bikes to each other so the cranks don't turn. The security cable is a very nice touch that I would have no problem trusting for cross town and short stops, but I still added a standard, coated bike cable to secure it to the rack to feel more comfortable stopping overnight as the provided cable could very easily be cut with a small bolt cutter. Load your heavier bike on first to reduce the leverage placed on the rack. Take a short test run before going a long distance.
text_fidelity_b: Thule 9001 Raceway 2 Bike Trunk Mounted Bike Rack, Black, One Size
